newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat prices under pressure, demand slow.
newsitem.headline: German wheat prices under pressure, demand slow.

text.p: German spot wheat prices are falling in thin trades in both the cash and export markets, brokers said on Tuesday.
"The only feature has been some inquiry from southern European millers but they have not yet bought anything," a broker in Hamburg said.
New crop bread wheat has eased amid reports of a return to favourable crop weather in southern Europe and Britain after a dry spell in March/April.
But brokers said the rains were received late and the drought did reduce crop expectations.
Markets would take direction from crop progress news in June and July.
German producers would not release any discounted wheat prior to the harvest as they were still optimistic on prices.
Feed wheat markets came under pressure from British offers.
Trading in barley and rye was extremely quiet.
The Hamburg grain exchange cut its spot bread wheat price (12.5 percent protein, 220 hagberg) by 2.50 marks/tonne on the week to 282.50 marks but left the feed wheat price at 280.
Fob Baltic sellers cut nominal May delivery wheat by between 1.50 and 2.50 marks on the week.
They quoted 12 percent protein wheat at 277.50-296.50 marks and material with 13/14 percent protein at 285-315 marks.
Fob Baltic barley offers were unchanged at 272.50 marks, off 1.00. Rye was down by up to 2.50 marks at 265-270.
New crop sellers cut nominal wheat prices by 2.50-5.00 marks.
Fob Baltic September wheat with 12 percent protein was at parity with May at 277.50 marks.
New crop rye indications are at around 265 marks and barley was set at 242.50-257.50, depending on port and shipment date.
